To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
regular code can be understood with less time and effort than non-regular code, but not by reading repeated code segments more quickly.

(1) regular code is read more quickly and more easily than non-regular code, (2) the time and effort needed to read regular code segments decreases with the distance of the segments from the beginning of the sequence, (3) the time and number of fixations needed to read regular segments do not decrease with the distance from the beginning of a sequence, and (4) reading regular code is not purely linear, but exhibits significant variability across subjects.

regular code segments are indeed read faster and more easily than non-regular ones with the same functionality; however, the speedup is not due to reading repeated segments more quickly, but rather to spending more time on the initial segment and then skimming later ones.
